newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: ROWING-GERMANY WIN INAUGURAL WORLD CUP.
newsitem.headline: ROWING-GERMANY WIN INAUGURAL WORLD CUP.

text.p: Germany won the inaugural rowing World Cup on Sunday and sealed a triumphant day by also lifting the Lucerne regatta trophy.
The German national team went into the final regatta of the three-event series with a commanding overall lead and extended it with five victories in the 14 boat classes to win both prizes.
The wins came in the men's quadruple sculls and lightweight double sculls, the women's double and quadruple sculls, and in the men's eight.
In the final overall standings, Germany amassed 209 points ahead of Britain on 101 and Romania on 88.
Romania won two boat classes with the other seven divided between Belarus, Britain, Canada, Denmark, Italy, Lithuania and Slovenia.

The dream team British coxless four of four-time Olympic champion Steve Redgrave, double Olympic champion Matthew Pinsent, Tim Foster and James Cracknell produced an awesome perfomance for a third successive World Cup victory.
The Romanian four got the fastest start but the British took the lead before the 500 metre mark and by halfway were 0.79 up on the Romanians.

They moved away again to open up a 1.70 second gap by 1,500 metres and then put in a devastating demonstration of sheer power at 1,750 metres, with strokeman Pinsent moving the rate up to 43 strokes a minute, to take an immediate length out of the Romanians.
The British crew crossed the line in 5:53.09, over two seconds clear of the Romanians.
Pinsent said afterwards: "We rowed in a very controlled way when we were 3/4 and then one length up. It put us in a position to row on, do the business and carry it off."
The Lucerne final was the eighth successive win for the undefeated British four formed in April this year.

The French crew, who pushed the British to the line in Paris three weeks ago, finished third. The French could not live with the pace and despite a strong late burst were 2.52 seconds behind at the finish.

It was a clean sweep of three World Cup victories for the winners of the single sculls. The men's title went to Iztok Cop of Slovenia and Olympic champion Katya Khodotovitch from Belarus won the women's event.
In a close race to the line behind Cop, World Cup newcomer Rob Waddell from New Zealand just lost out to the experienced Frederik Bekken of Norway.

One of the pre-race favourites, Ibrahim Ali of Egypt, who this season became the first rower from the African continent to win international medals with two second places in the World Cup, had a bad day and finished last.

The Danish lightweight four of Thomas Ebert, Thomas Poulsen, Eskild Ebbesen and Victor Feddersen, three of whom won Olympic gold in Atlanta, also made it three World Cup wins in a row with a two second margin over their nearest challengers, Germany 1.

"The inaugural World Cup has been a huge hit with the federations, rowers and coaches and is the first truly global competition for rowing outside the World Championships," said Matt Smith, executive director of the International Rowing Federation.

"Twenty-six nations qualified for today's finals illustrating the worldwide support for the competition. We've enjoyed a very high quality of racing which has been televised in all five continents. The World Cup has generated big media interest with record TV audiences and hours of coverage for rowing."
